items.title: Researchers develop 3D-printable humanoid robotic hand costing less than $650
items.summary: Researchers developed the PHD-Hand, a five-fingered humanoid robotic hand costing under $650 to manufacture using 3D printing. This design utilizes a linkage-driven mechanism instead of tendon-based systems to improve dexterity, reliability, and reduced complexity. The hand features 15 independently actuated degrees of freedom and bidirectional movement, based on TPU hinges and spring steel drive rods. Prototypes have successfully demonstrated 33 grasp types and the ability to manipulate various everyday objects. The team plans to release the design files and software as open-source resources to make advanced robotic manipulation more accessible.

This advancement signals a potential democratization of advanced robotic manipulation capabilities across various sectors of the technology industry.

items.title: Egyptian underwater robotics team inspires award-winning education startup
items.summary: An Egyptian underwater robotics team developed an educational technology venture that won first place at Louisiana Tech University’s 2026 Top Dog New Venture Championship. The team, Overflow Robotics, achieved a notable fifth-place finish at the MATE ROV World Championship. They established Tech in Schools, an educational program that teaches middle and high school students engineering and robotics through practical projects. This initiative aims to build student confidence by allowing learners to design, build, and troubleshoot real robots. The founders plan to expand this program and their venture into other regions.

items.title: China Post tests 45 Robotera humanoids for parcel handling
items.summary: China Post is testing 45 Robotera humanoids for parcel handling at its Hangzhou Postal District Center. The trial involves tasks such as picking up, orienting, and placing parcels of varying sizes and shapes onto induction platforms. Testing began in April 2026, focusing on parcel recognition and placement amidst the repetitive sorting line work. Robotera reported throughput increases from 500 to 1,200 parcels per hour during test periods with over 90% operational accuracy. Conflicting reports exist regarding the throughput figures and the scope of the reported efficiency.

items.title: Volvo Cars Begins Training Hexagon’s AEON Humanoids at Ghent Plant Ahead of 2027 Production Target
items.summary: Volvo Cars has introduced Hexagon Robotics' AEON humanoid robots to its Ghent, Belgium factory for initial task training. The robots are currently learning through imitation learning, beginning with precise component placement before scaling to more complex tasks. A broader factory pilot involving additional units is planned for the first half of 2027, aiming for live production deployment by mid-2027. AEON robots feature a wheeled-leg architecture, allowing them to navigate and handle payloads efficiently on factory floors. This deployment expands AEON's presence in the automotive sector, following similar trials by BMW and Schaeffler.

items.title: The Sequence Robotics - Issue #981: How NVIDIA Isaac Turns Practice Into Robot Skills
items.summary: NVIDIA Isaac functions as a development loop for teaching robots physical skills through a structured process. This involves building virtual tasks in Isaac Sim, generating policies with Isaac Lab from experience, and using pretrained models like GR00T. The process connects learned actions to physical machines using Isaac ROS and Isaac OS to maintain a responsive control loop. Physical trials then feed errors back into OSMO-coordinated experiments for iterative improvement. Ultimately, Isaac's value is in simplifying the practice-evaluate-deploy iteration for complex robotic tasks.

The methodology involves building virtual tasks within Isaac Sim, generating policies using Isaac Lab based on experience and pretrained models like GR00T, and connecting learned actions to physical machines utilizing Isaac ROS and Isaac OS to establish a responsive control loop. Physical trials then feed resulting errors back into OSMO-coordinated experiments for iterative refinement of the skills. This system effectively bridges simulation and reality to guide robotic learning. This advancement signifies a streamlined approach for deploying complex physical skills in autonomous robotic systems.

items.title: Neura Robotics partners with Costa Group to develop Aragón’s physical AI ambitions
items.summary: Neura Robotics, Costa Group, and the Aragón regional government are collaborating to develop an industrial ecosystem for physical AI. This initiative aims to translate existing industrial expertise into commercially valuable robotic capabilities. The project will establish Neura Gym Aragón, a facility combining robotics, AI models, and simulation for training. This zone will allow companies to test and develop robotic applications using their specific operational knowledge. The collaboration seeks to bridge the gap between digital intelligence and physical world performance, particularly in sectors like agriculture.

items.title: Lute raises $20 million to give robots a sense of touch
items.summary: Lute, a physical AI startup, raised $20 million to advance foundation models that allow robots to use tactile information alongside visual data. This technology addresses limitations in current physical AI by incorporating tactile sensing for understanding grip force and material properties. The company developed Lute-0, a video-action model that learns scene changes for robotic movements, demonstrating superior performance in manipulation tasks. Lute is deploying its technology in retail and logistics, guiding system integrators in deploying physical AI. The funding will be used to expand data acquisition, improve models, and extend commercial operations.
